name: Laurence Salcedo
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember the first porch I could reach after surgery.” People around the approach to Seabright Court know Laurence by a small Monday habit. Laurence likes to watch the beach traffic thin enough for workers going the other way.
voice: I needed somewhere to sit on my way home after surgery. They left that chair outside for a whole season.
appearance: Laurence has short copper curls, an aquiline nose and a square chin, and a favorite piece of clothing, a soft blue checked shirt. It usually goes with a narrow brass watch set a little fast. When somebody else has the floor, Laurence gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in.
personality: Laurence tells a better story in a kitchen than at a microphone. Family members sometimes underestimate how far Laurence will go to back a quiet opinion once it is actually challenged.
agenda: To leave a resting chair outside for the next recovering walker.
family: Cameron Kelly is Laurence’s half-sibling. Laurence keeps the photographs. Cameron knows which ones can be shared. They enjoy remembering people in public and also know what it feels like to have a private afternoon turned into an anecdote for strangers. Asked about *The guarantee*, Cameron says, “I want to downsize while the house is still ours to choose.”
connections: Grey Lopez. A resting place proves more useful than an empty porch someone always envied.

reactions.situation: Two visitors bid against each other for the porch chair
reactions.response: Laurence asks whether both people want the object itself or a particular memory of it.

reactions.situation: A stranger offers money to cut ahead of an exhausted neighbor
reactions.response: Laurence keeps the neighbor's place and finds out whether the stranger needs a different kind of help.

reactions.situation: If a relative makes a joke at a child's expense
reactions.response: Laurence repeats the child's actual point and waits for a reply to that.
